title: How long does it take to form a habit?
text:
For years, self-help books have repeated that a new habit takes twenty-one days to form. The figure goes back to a plastic surgeon {A}, and it was never meant as a scientific rule. When researchers at a London university followed ninety-six volunteers who tried to adopt small daily routines, they found that the average time was closer to two months {B}.

The differences between individuals were striking. Some people made an action automatic in under three weeks, {C}. Surprisingly, missing a single day did little harm; the chances of success fell only when several days were skipped {D}.

What does this mean for the rest of us? Psychologists suggest linking the new behaviour to something we already do, {E}. Equally important is to start with a task {F}. The real aim is not the first week but the months that follow. Those who understand this tend to be far more forgiving of themselves, and that attitude, researchers argue, is half of the battle.
